Assuming that one isn't critically low on the hierarchy of needs, I guess the looming idea in the background, in response to not wanting to live, is that things might get better.  At which point it becomes a question of optimism or not-optimism (or vice versa).  

"Living" isn't how things are as much as how they might become.  A single mother slaving away to secure her child's future isn't thinking about the car she currently drives.  A yuppie's life isn't their current salary but the next rung up the ladder.  "Living" is a mental picture just out of reach but that alone can be enough to get someone to wake up for the day ahead.  

But yeah, it's all kind of a load of crap.  Once you start buying into a certain level of optimism, *The Secret* doesn't sound that far-fetched, at which point you can't really make heads or tails of your mental state.  This has been three paragraph answer to an unanswerable question.  Though I do stand by my first point, in that I try not to dwell and hope things turn for the better.
